screens.title: Which deletion hurts?
screens.text: Both 10 and 50 are leaves. Which deletion makes the tree unbalanced?
screens.reveal: Deleting 10 leaves node 20 with an empty left branch and a right branch of height 1, so its balance factor becomes 1 − (−1) = +2.

screens.title: Goal
screens.text: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to delete a leaf from an AVL tree and restore the AVL property. This app covers leaf deletion only. Deleting a node with children (delete by copying) will be covered in the lecture.

task.stem: How do you delete a leaf from a BST?
task.hint: This question checks leaf deletion. When a leaf is removed, no other node moves until the balance factors have been checked.

options.explanation: The parent stays where it is. Only the leaf is removed.

options.text: Move its sibling into its place.
options.explanation: The sibling stays where it is. Only the leaf is removed.

options.text: Remove it, so that its parent's branch becomes empty.

screens.title: Deleting 50: no rotation needed
screens.text: Remove the leaf, and then update the balance factors from its parent up to the root.
steps: 50 is a leaf, so it is removed.
Node 40 now has a balance factor of −1 − 0 = −1.
Node 20 now has a balance factor of 1 − 0 = +1.
Every node now has a balance factor of −1, 0 or +1.

screens.title: Deleting 10: one rotation
screens.text: This is the same tree, but now 10 is deleted.
screens.caption: Node 20 has a balance factor of +2, and its right child, 40, has a balance factor of 0. A single left rotation about 20 fixes it.
steps: 10 is a leaf, so it is removed.
Node 20 now has a balance factor of 1 − (−1) = +2.
Node 20 has a balance factor of +2, so it is unbalanced.
Rotate 40 around 20. This is a left rotation about 20.
Every node now has a balance factor of −1, 0 or +1.

screens.title: Leaf deletion
points: 2. Update the balance factors from its parent up to the root.
3. If a node has a balance factor of +2 and its right child has 0 or +1, do a single left rotation about that node.
4. If a node has a balance factor of −2 and its left child has 0 or −1, do a single right rotation about that node.
If the child leans the other way, a double rotation is needed. The examples in this app avoid that case, and the lecture covers it.
screens.showRule: Remove the leaf, update the balance factors up to the root, and rotate towards the shorter branch.

screens.title: Worked example: the mirror case
screens.caption: Node 30 has a balance factor of −2, and its left child, 20, has a balance factor of 0. A single right rotation about 30 fixes it.
steps: 40 is a leaf, so it is removed.
Node 30 now has a balance factor of −1 − 1 = −2.
Node 30 has a balance factor of −2, so it is unbalanced.
Rotate 20 around 30. This is a right rotation about 30.
Every node now has a balance factor of −1, 0 or +1.

task.stem: Delete 30 and rebalance the tree. Build the final tree.
task.hint: This question checks rebalancing after a deletion. At the unbalanced node, a single rotation towards the shorter branch restores the balance.

feedback.correct: After 30 is removed, node 50 has a balance factor of +2, and its right child, 70, has +1. A single left rotation about 50 gives 70(50, 80).
feedback.incorrect: After 30 is removed, node 50 has a balance factor of +2, and its right child, 70, has +1. A single left rotation about 50 gives 70(50, 80).

task.stem: 80 has just been deleted. Enter the new balance factors of 70 and 50.
task.hint: This question checks whether you can update balance factors after a deletion. Start at the parent of the removed leaf and work up to the root.

wrongAnswers.feedback: The sign is reversed. The balance factor is the height of the right branch minus the height of the left branch. Node 50 has a right branch of height 0 and a left branch of height 1, so its balance factor is 0 − 1 = −1. A taller left branch gives a negative number.
That is the balance factor that node 50 had before the deletion. After a leaf is removed, update every node on the path up to the root.

feedback.correct: Node 70 is a leaf. Both of its branches are empty, with height −1, so its balance factor is −1 − (−1) = 0. Node 50 has a right branch of height 0 and a left branch of height 1, so its balance factor is 0 − 1 = −1.
feedback.incorrect: Node 70 is a leaf. Both of its branches are empty, with height −1, so its balance factor is −1 − (−1) = 0. Node 50 has a right branch of height 0 and a left branch of height 1, so its balance factor is 0 − 1 = −1.

screens.title: Lesson check
screens.text: This check has one question for each assessment criterion of the lesson's objective. You can re-attempt each question once, and the Hint button is always available.

screens.title: Summary
points: A leaf is simply removed, and nothing else moves.
Update the balance factors from the parent up to the root.
At a node with a balance factor of +2 or −2, rotate towards the shorter branch.
